races.title: State House, District 94
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Blair Eddins
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House for District 94 since October 2024, when district Republicans picked him to replace Jeffrey Elmore. Former auditor, farmer and small business owner. Works at Samaritan's Purse in North Wilkesboro. NC State graduate (1995).

endorsements.text: In his 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Eddins listed these endorsers himself: NC Values, North Carolina Grassroots Government, Robert Duncan, Rev. John Triplett, Susan Sturgill, Pastor Kevin Brown, Kevin Holland and Kyle Lamb. Ballotpedia did not independently identify endorsements for 2024 or 2026.

cands.gaps: We could not find his exact birthplace, the county of his family farm, or the years he worked as an auditor or ran his businesses. The page listing the bills he sponsored was empty, so no sponsored bills could be confirmed. We found no documented actions or stated positions on data centers, development or growth limits, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, police pay, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site mentions real estate development as a past business, but we found no public statement from him on development policy. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. We found no controversies in the pages reviewed.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign site says he was born into a North Carolina farming family and grew up on the family farm, and he earned his degree at North Carolina State University; the exact birthplace is not given.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since October 2024. Earlier career as an auditor, farmer, and owner of grading, landscaping and real estate development businesses; now works at Samaritan's Purse.
qual.why: Current legislative service plus an auditing career and business ownership place him in the high range, though his time in the House is short.
qual.label: Current legislative service plus an auditing career and business ownership place him in the high range, though his time in the House is short.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says the right to keep and bear arms is 'non-negotiable' and that elected officials must never restrict it.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says the legislature should embrace 'life-affirming protections for mothers and their unborn children.' In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said he is committed to protecting the life of the unborn.

cands.name: Andy Warren
cands.bio: Andy Warren was the Democratic nominee for North Carolina House District 94 in 2026. He lost the general election to incumbent Republican Blair Eddins. The pages reviewed give no information on his occupation or earlier offices.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as endorsed by the voter guide 'Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy' (Sway voting group by Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Andy Warren was born or raised, when he came to North Carolina, his occupation, or any earlier elected office. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, and his campaign website showed only a slogan and an election countdown, so we found no stated positions on data centers, property taxes, development, immigration, guns, abortion, schools, policing or campaign money. We found no documented actions, controversies or foreign ties.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
